model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), holdco look-through: core banking and insurance profit attributable to DSFH after the 25.63% DSBG minority, payout-constrained retention, net debt zero, Bank of Chongqing stake at market in the bridge

equity_bridge.item: Bank of Chongqing stake at H-share market price, DSFH look-through share
equity_bridge.note: Group holding 13.48% after buying 30.0M H shares on 24 Jun 2026 (0440.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:866-869). Implied holding is about 489M shares: 13.20% of the ~3,477M pre-conversion shares, plus 30M. Value 489M x HK$8.295 (1963.HK close 2026-10-09) = HK$4,056M, against a carrying amount of HK$3,597M. The stake is held by Dah Sing Bank inside DSBG, so DSFH's share is 74.37% = HK$3,017M (HK$9.46/share). Priced on the H line, which is conservative: the A line, 601963.SS at CNY10.91 x 1.1721, is about HK$12.79, a 54% premium. BOCQ trades near 0.5x its own book.

equity_bridge.item: Jointly controlled entities (Bank Consortium Holding, 13.33%) at book, look-through
equity_bridge.note: Carrying HK$167.8M at 30 Jun 2026 x 74.37%. JCE results (TTM about HK$38M) are excluded from the flow.

equity_bridge.item: CET1 surplus above a ~15.5% peer level: NOT credited in the base
equity_bridge.note: DSB CET1 is 19.1% against HKMA minimum-plus-buffers of roughly 10-11% and HK mid-tier peers at 15-17%. The surplus is about HK$5-6bn at DSB, HK$3.7-4.5bn look-through (HK$12-14/share). It has risen for two years without a buyback under family control, so a minority holder cannot count on it. It is released only in the bull path (lower retention in years 1-3). Recorded at 0 deliberately, not omitted.

historical_growth.fcf_cagr_basis: Reported FCF is meaningless for a bank (deposit and loan flows run through OCF). The FCF CAGR fields therefore carry attributable profit: FY2020 1,158.2 -> FY2025 2,056.9 (5yr) and FY2022 1,224.4 -> FY2025 (3yr). SBC is immaterial, so the owner-basis adjustment does not move them.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (shareholders' funds FY2020 28,386 -> FY2025 37,490). Revenue 3yr is 5.8%, but FY2022-25 includes the HIBOR up-cycle. The 5-year EPS and profit CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID trough. Forward base revenue growth is 3-4.5%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.7% 5yr) diverges by more than 30% from EPS CAGR (12.3% 5yr, 19.0% 3yr). EPS recovers from the FY2020 trough (HK$3.62) and benefits from FY2023-25 rate-driven NIM expansion. Equity compounds more slowly because about 40% is paid out, and OCI and FX swings run through reserves. Neither number is a clean forward rate. The base uses 3-4.5% revenue growth, roughly ROE x retention on the core book.
historical_growth.notes: Credit costs more than doubled from about HK$0.73bn (FY2023) to HK$1.78bn (FY2024, FY2025, TTM). The FY2024-25 profit growth came from NIM and fees despite that, so normalisation of credit cost is the main earnings lever in every scenario.

scenario_narratives.base: Credit costs normalise gradually from the HKCRE peak, NIM holds about 2.4%, and wealth and SME fees carry growth. The Wong family keeps paying about 45% of earnings and keeps the CET1 surplus. Core ROE stays about 7.5%, below the 11% CoE. Value is roughly 0.45-0.5x book: the core franchise is worth less than book, plus the BOCQ stake at market.
scenario_narratives.bull: HKCRE troughs, credit cost falls to about 0.6% of loans, core ROE approaches 9%, and the group releases about half its look-through CET1 surplus through special dividends or buybacks. The holdco discount narrows toward DSBG's own rating.
scenario_narratives.bear: A second HKCRE leg, Mainland developer defaults and faster HIBOR cuts drive a year-2 earnings trough and further BCM write-downs. Payout stays at 40% while ROE sits about 6%, so the trapped capital earns well below its cost.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A small Hong Kong bank holdco valued on what a minority holder receives. The core banking and insurance flow attributable to DSFH, after the 25.63% DSBG minority, is capitalised at an 11% HKD cost of equity, with retention set at the family's demonstrated payout. The Bank of Chongqing associate is valued at market on the H line, not on its equity-accounted earnings. The holdco discount comes from the payout constraint and the uncredited CET1 surplus, not from an arbitrary percentage.
key_risks_to_valuation: HKCRE credit losses: every scenario's margin path depends on credit cost normalising from 1.2% of loans
HIBOR/NIM sensitivity: NII is about 70% of operating income
Capital allocation is controlled by the Wong family: the CET1 surplus may never be released (base assumes it is not)
BOCQ value is marked to a thinly traded H line and to Chongqing/Mainland credit; it is about 20% of base value
BCM Macau structural decline and further goodwill or impairment charges
Engine terminal value relies on a 3% HKD nominal growth rate and an 11% CoE; core ROE is below CoE, so value is sensitive to the spread

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 33.08-51.20. Look-through cross-checks used 2356.HK, 1963.HK, 601963.SS and CNYHKD=X closes on the same date.
data_sources.financials: 0440.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, HKD millions); 0440.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt income statement and note 25 (BOCQ); 0440.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt income statement, balance sheet, note 10 (BOCQ deemed disposal and stake purchase), segment note 30, capital ratios and directors' interests.
data_sources.qualitative: 0440.HK_Analysis.json (2026 analysis: HKCRE, BCM, holdco structure, guidance).

inputs.share_count_basis: Basic weighted ordinary shares for H1-26 of 319,084,493 (0440.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:945; 319.1M at FY2025). Held FLAT. There have been no buybacks since FY2019 (HK$592M), and SBC is tiny (HK$21M FY2025) and expensed in the flow. Diluted EPS (HK$4.31 vs basic HK$4.57 in H1-26) is lower because of the potential dilution of DSFH's share of associate profit from the Bank of Chongqing convertible bond, not because of any DSFH share issuance. That associate is valued at market in equity_bridge, outside the flow, so the dilution is already priced.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual share-based compensation of HK$21.3M (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp; FY2024 19.9M, FY2023 14.2M). Interims do not disclose it, so the FY2025 figure stands in for the TTM. Immaterial: 0.25% of revenue. It nets out of the bank flow, because ebitda includes it and sbc_pct removes it. last_fcf = TTM core profit attributable to DSFH shareholders, excluding the Bank of Chongqing associate and one-offs (derivation in notes). reported_fcf = last_fcf + SBC.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases FY2020-H1-26 (ShareRepurchases = 0 in every period since the FY2019 HK$592M). Distribution is dividends only: FY2025 DPS HK$2.58 (+23%), HK$747M paid in FY2025 cash flow, HK$453M paid in H1-26. Interim FY2026 DPS HK$1.20 (vs HK$1.16).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; Friday close, markets shut over the weekend of the valuation date)
inputs.wacc_rationale: HKD cost of equity of 11.0%. The HKD is pegged to the USD and long HKD government yields track USTs at roughly 3.7-4.0%. Add a beta of about 0.9 x 6.0% ERP = 5.4%, plus about 1.5% for size, family control and Hong Kong CRE concentration, and round to 11.0%. That sits above HSBC (10.5%, global diversified) and LYG (10.0%), which fits a small HK lender with a ~HK$23bn HKCRE book and a Macau subsidiary in structural decline. The rate is in the currency of the flows. One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable. The bank flow is after all operating expenses, including premises depreciation and lease charges inside 'Operating expenses'. No separate lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. DSFH owns 74.37% of Dah Sing Banking Group (2356.HK; directors' interests, 0440.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:5612). NCI profit of HK$456M in H1-26 is exactly 25.63% of DSBG's HK$1,780.5M. TTM NCI is 634.5 - 404.7 + 456.3 = 686.2. Strip out the NCI share of the Bank of Chongqing items (25.63% x (797.4 associate - 125.3 deemed-disposal loss) = 172.3, excluded from the flow) and add back its share of the DSBG-level BCM goodwill impairment (25.63% x 493.0 = 126.4, a one-off). That leaves NCI on core DSBG profit of 640.3, which is 767 pre-tax at 16.5%, or 24.8% of core pre-tax profit. Every 'ebitda' margin below is core pre-tax margin x 0.752 + SBC%, so the flow is profit attributable to DSFH ordinary holders, and NCI equity (HK$9.27bn) is NOT also deducted in the bridge. DSFH's directly held insurance and investment operations (Dah Sing Insurance, Macau Insurance, Macau Pension Fund; segment PAT HK$145M in H1-26, net segment assets about HK$8.9bn) are 100% owned and sit inside the flow without an NCI deduction.
inputs.holdco_treatment: The qualitative analyst asked whether a holdco discount or SOTP is warranted. It is handled in the flow, not as a percentage haircut. The flow is what a DSFH minority holder actually receives. In the base case retention is set at the Wong family's demonstrated payout of about 42-45% of earnings, not at the lower retention a CET1 target would need. DSB's CET1 has risen from 16.9% (FY2024) to 18.8% (FY2025) and 19.1% (H1-26) with no buyback, and the existing surplus over a ~15-16% peer level (about HK$5-6bn at DSB, HK$12-14 per DSFH share look-through) is NOT credited in the base. That excess retention and the uncredited surplus are the economic content of the holdco discount. Adding a further % discount on top would count it twice. Market cross-check: 74.37% x 1,405.75M DSBG shares x HK$14.16 = HK$14.8bn, which is above DSFH's own market cap (HK$14.0bn at inputs.price_as_of) before counting ~HK$8.9bn of net insurance and investment assets. So DSFH trades at about a 40% discount to look-through value at market, on top of DSBG's own ~0.55x P/B. That is the 0087.HK pattern, and it is why the bull case is a capital-release case and not a margin case.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, with net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book. The house precedent for banks (LYG, HSBC, WF, BCS, NAB.AX, USB, WFC) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route: same economics, expressed as distributable cash. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry. Deposits (HK$204.0bn) are operating funding, not debt. Subordinated notes (HK$4.3bn Tier 2) are regulatory capital and wholesale funding; their coupons already sit in interest expense, so they are not deducted. OCF is meaningless for a bank (the CSV swings from -4.9bn to +11.4bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = 'Total operating income' (excludes associate and JCE results). TTM = FY25 8,266.9 - H1-25 4,112.4 + H1-26 4,318.3 = 8,472.8. Opex TTM 3,577.1 - 1,781.7 + 1,805.4 = 3,600.8 (cost/income 42.5%; H1-26 41.8%). Credit impairment TTM 1,783.4 - 729.2 + 724.1 = 1,778.4 (21.0% of revenue, about 1.2% of the HK$147.6bn loan book, elevated by HKCRE downgrades and collateral revaluations). Core pre-tax profit = 3,093.6 (36.5% margin). EXCLUDED from the flow: share of Bank of Chongqing results (TTM 797.4; valued at market in the bridge instead, because DSFH only receives BOCQ cash dividends, HK$207M in FY2025, and BOCQ retained earnings are excluded from DSB capital), the deemed-disposal loss on BOCQ CB conversions (-125.3), the FY2025 HK$493.0M non-cash BCM goodwill impairment, investment-property fair-value moves, and JCE results (bridge at book). 'ebitda' = core PBT 3,093.6 + SBC 21.3 - grossed-up NCI 767 = 2,348 (27.7%). Cash tax 16.5% (HK profits tax; H1-26 tax 295.7 on PBT ex-associate/JCE/deemed of 1,802.8 = 16.4%). FY0 check: (2,348 - 21.3) x 0.835 = 1,943 core attributable profit. Reconciliation to reported TTM attributable profit of 2,108.3: + BOCQ attributable 74.37% x 672.1 = 499.8, - goodwill attributable 366.6, - deemed disposal and other small items. 'capex' = capital retention = retention fraction x attributable profit margin. D&A = 0, because depreciation is inside opex.

bear.margin_rationale: Faster HIBOR cuts compress NIM back toward 2.1-2.2%, and a second HKCRE leg plus Mainland developer stress push credit cost to about HK$2.2bn in year 2. BCM in Macau needs further write-downs. Core pre-tax margin troughs at 32% and recovers only to 39.5% (credit cost about 15% of revenue, cost/income 45.5%). Core attributable ROE settles about 6%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention is 60% of attributable profit (payout 40%, the FY2025 level) through year 5 as the family protects capital, then fades to 50%.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) is +4%. H1-26 operating income was +5.0% y/y: NII +6.5% with NIM at 2.44%, fees +29%, and trading income halved. HIBOR easing caps NII growth, and wealth and SME fees carry it. Growth is 4-4.5% in years 2-5, about ROE x retention, then fades to 3% HKD nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Core pre-tax margin (before NCI) is 39.5% in year 1. H1-26 ran at 41.4%, but H2 credit charges are seasonally heavier (H2-25 HK$1.05bn vs H1-26 HK$0.72bn). It rises to 44.5% by year 5 as credit cost normalises from 21% of revenue (about 1.2% of loans) to about 13% (about 0.7% of loans, the FY2022-23 level), with cost/income held at 42.5%. Management reports impaired HKCRE loans falling from HK$2,177M to HK$1,697M over the year to mid-2026. The ebitda margin is core margin x 0.752 (after the 25.63% DSBG minority) + 0.25% SBC. Year-5 core attributable ROE is about 7.5% on core equity, below the 11% CoE, so the core franchise is worth less than its book.
base.capex_rationale: Retention is 55% of attributable profit in years 1-2 (payout 45%, vs the demonstrated 40-42%), fading to 45% by year 10. That is the level a 3% terminal growth rate needs at a ~7% ROE (g/ROE = 43%). capex% = retention x attributable margin, where attributable margin = (ebitda% - 0.25) x 0.835. Years 1-5 over-retain relative to a CET1-target FCFE. That is deliberate: it models the family-controlled payout a minority holder actually receives.
base.tax_rationale: HK profits tax 16.5%. H1-26 effective rate on PBT excluding associate, JCE and deemed-disposal items was 16.4%.

bull.margin_rationale: HKCRE has troughed (Grade-A leasing and vacancy improving, per H1-26 prospects). Credit cost falls to about 11% of revenue (about 0.6% of loans) by year 4, and cost/income edges to 41.5%. Core pre-tax margin reaches 47.5%, and core attributable ROE about 8.5-9%.
bull.capex_rationale: Capital release. Retention is set at growth-required levels (45% of attributable profit, falling to 40%), and about HK$1.8bn of the look-through CET1 surplus (roughly half) is distributed over years 1-3 through special dividends or a buyback, about HK$600M a year, so capex% is cut by about 6-7 points in years 1-3. This is the case where the holdco discount narrows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13.5x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%, and bull cut from 35% to 25%. The ~HK$23bn HKCRE book is in a multi-year downturn, and FY2024-25 credit costs were 2.4x the FY2023 level. The Macau subsidiary is in structural decline (FY2025 goodwill impairment). The bull depends on a capital-release decision that only the controlling family can make, and it has not made one since the FY2019 buyback. Symmetric 25/50/25, in line with the HSBC and BCS bank precedent.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
